variants.file: 方案1-院前弯路与小路口.png
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: NEW village layout option for a Chinese rural pixel-art game, portrait 2:3 composition, whole village visible, crisp chunky pixel art, elevated near-orthographic bird's-eye view. This is a clear layout illustration for choosing a plan.
Reference image 1: ORIGINAL REAL GEOGRAPHIC POSITION MAP, use only to understand the relative positions and connectivity; redraw every element independently, do not reproduce smartphone UI, green map tiles, map markers or text.
Reference image 2: ARCHITECTURAL IDENTITY ONLY for Ayu family house, independently redraw blue roof / cream upper floor with balcony / red brick lower floor / left garage / right front door, no pixel extraction or pasted pieces.
CRITICAL CORRECTION: the actual village is on ONE BROAD LEVEL FLAT valley floor BETWEEN low hills. The inhabitable village, ALL houses, orchards, courtyards, streets and wheat fields share a flat level ground plane. Never place houses or farms up slopes. NO terraces, NO stepped topography, NO retaining-wall platforms, NO stairways between houses, NO hillside settlement, NO visible rising terrain through the village. Surrounding low wooded hills ONLY at the very distant top and outer edges, gently receding blue-green mountains behind them. Large open flat meadow gaps and flat agricultural land inside the valley make the level geography unmistakable. Same-size homes across the layout, avoid strong cinematic perspective scaling.
Preserve original-map core neighboring relations with north at top: a relative's home at far north; Ayu old ancestral home south of that; Daba home farther south slightly west of this northern pair. The winding north approach reaches the CENTRAL junction near Ayu home. Ayu plot slightly LEFT of middle junction, 5A neighbor to its WEST, 2A neighbor to its NORTHEAST/EAST. South of Ayu: 3A, then 8A, then 4A at the lower south end. 6A is east of 3A, 7A farther east/southeast. About twenty modest distinct rural houses including these core homes, remaining homes form irregular small groups along the west and east. Do not arrange houses into aligned rectangular rows or equal-spaced grid.
Ayu: exactly ONE recognizable blue-roof cream/redbrick two-floor house, a coherent complete property with FRONT and REAR trees and orchard, dense rear leafy woods directly behind, several fruit trees both sides of front yard, a clear front gate and entrance route, a side footpath connecting front and rear without going through building. Keep this identity and yard structure consistent across the three plans. Trees shelter the plot, not block the gate. This landmark should be readable and large enough to find at central-left.
All assets newly drawn; no extraction from old Ayu maps. Abundant lush summer tree crowns, intense warm midday sunshine, deep cool canopy shadows, dense golden wheat on flat fields, some garden flowers, a small communal lotus pond separate from Ayu orchard, a modest stream near the eastern edge. The stream is shallow and on flat banks, no waterfalls or cliff canyon. Distant faint heat haze only, foreground pixels stay sharp.
Road geometry: gentle real bends shaped by property boundaries and trees, irregular soft junctions, uneven widths, short local straight approaches allowed but NO ruler-straight arterial roads and NO regular rectangular road grid. Connected walkable road network. Worn pale ochre earth and a little old stone, modest rural scale, no urban boulevards. A clear northern entry, eastern exit and southern entry. No people, cars, UI, labels, numbers, legends, text or watermark; no collage or panels.

PLAN A: keep the original real-map branching structure closest. One sinuous north-south lane comes down from the northwest/north homes, bends past Ayu's FRONT gate near the middle, meeting a curving west-east lane at a modest asymmetric Y junction. A small irregular shaded gathering space is tucked just EAST of Ayu junction, with one large tree and a lotus pond farther northeast. South residential branch loosely follows 3A,8A,4A in a staggered chain. Flat wheatfields east and south. Small quiet front yards, narrow connecting footpaths. Do not build any circular ring boulevard.
